title: Tenant scoping on User
summary: User now carries a TenantID. Every user belongs to exactly one tenant — the foundation everything else builds on.
why: Multi-tenant separation requires every user to belong to exactly one tenant.
review_questions: Is TenantID set on every user creation path?
Are existing users backfilled with a TenantID?

title: New tenant-scoped APIKey model
summary: Adds an APIKey struct with bcrypt hash, last-used timestamp, and revocation timestamp. Keys are owned by tenants, not users.
why: Machine clients need tenant-scoped authentication without user JWTs.
review_questions: Are keys stored hashed (no plaintext at rest)?
Can keys be revoked in O(1)?
Why no expiration field — is rotation expected to be operational rather than enforced?

title: Auth middleware now checks API keys
summary: The middleware checks X-API-Key before falling back to JWT validation. validateAPIKey enforces the ck_ prefix and a minimum length of 32 characters.
why: API clients need non-user authentication. JWT path is preserved unchanged for human users.
review_questions: Can this bypass tenant permissions downstream of the middleware?
Is the JWT fallback preserved exactly as before?
Does the prefix check leak timing information for attacks?
Is rate-limiting applied per tenant on the API key path?

title: Tests cover both auth paths
summary: Adds tests for valid JWT, valid API key, and a rejected wrong-prefix API key.
why: Auth changes need regression coverage on both code paths so a future refactor cannot silently widen the gate.
review_questions: Is the rejected-prefix test exhaustive (empty key, wrong prefix, too-short key)?
Are there integration tests that exercise this through the full middleware chain, not just unit tests?
